learning_outcomes.text: Students determine the energy yield of typical types of wind and hydropower plants depending on local conditions.
Based on mechanics and electrical engineering, they compare different plant concepts.
They quantitatively and qualitatively assess the environmental impacts and material usage.
They determine the effects of feeding wind energy into the grid and comment on the resulting problems and possible remedies.
Students critically classify new plant concepts.

syllabus_topics: Physical principles of wind energy systems (lift, Betz's law, ...)
Generator concepts for wind energy systems
Control strategies for wind energy systems
Environmental factors of wind energy systems: sound, shadow, effect on animals, recycling, life cycle analysis, ...
Physical principles of hydropower plants (Bernoulli's theorem), special effects (cavitation, water hammer)
Typical designs of water turbines, entire hydropower plants and pumped-storage power plants
Legal basis for the promotion of wind power and hydropower
Volatility and how to deal with it
Alternative plant types for wind or hydropower and their evaluation

assessment_methods.method: Combined exam (study project work and oral exam)

assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the module examination. The grading's relevance for the final grade is determined according to the study and examination regulations (SPO).
